That conflicts with this returned-value definition in the multi-inference or fallback case this change addresses. threads.body: The new provider-side nesting guidance has no reference scenario demonstrating its span boundaries and usage. The OpenAI and Anthropic scenarios observe client SDK calls; Google GenAI's nested tool spans cover client-side execution, not provider-side inference. These do not establish how a model-serving library exposes the proposed nested operations. The reference requirements in `.github/instructions/evaluate-reference.instructions.md:7-9` require scenarios to back convention changes. Please add a runnable scenario around a model-serving library API with values read from that library, or defer the provider-side recording guidance.

threads.body: Grouping by `service.name` does not prevent double-counting within a provider. Its request span and nested inference spans can share the same service resource. If the request reports 100 tokens and its children total 100, summing that group yields 200. Please clarify that consumers must choose request-level or individual-inference accounting and avoid summing overlapping usage, even within one service. Update the model and regenerate the docs.

threads.body:
This feels unintuitive to me on a nested span. In the Anthropic Messages API, we already report token usage per server-side tool loop iteration. But the OTEL span for each iteration would then have the total, and the total would be on both the span for the whole request and on its child spans, as opposed to the child spans adding up to the total. As a user if I see a nested inference span, I'd assume the tokens on that span are for that inference operation only.
Example trace for reference: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/opentelemetry#a-messages-api-request

replies.body: how would instrumentation for client SDK know that someone under reported usage already?

it can't. It's on observability platforms and the user to use appropriate filters in their dashboards to avoid double counting.

But some users may _want_ to see the fine-grained token usage of each iteration of the server-side tool loop, which they can't if instrumentations follow this added sentence here (if I understand it correctly, I'm interpreting "whole request" to mean the whole Messages API request).
